headline: China's memory maker CXMT says it will launch server memory on a denser new chip design before the end of 2026, years ahead of Samsung's reported 2028 plan.
score_reason: Curator score 6 lowered by 1: the 2026 launch and the lead over Samsung are CXMT's own claim, with no product shipped and no independent check.
importance_line: If CXMT delivers, Chinese rivals would close in on Samsung, SK hynix and Micron, the three firms that dominate memory chips, but nothing has shipped and the timing is the company's own claim.
source: Wccftech, citing CXMT president Cao Kanyu's conference speech
summary: Wccftech reports that CXMT's president, Cao Kanyu, told a chip conference in Shanghai that the Chinese memory maker will launch, before the end of 2026, a DDR5 server memory module built on the new 4F² design, in which each memory cell is stacked vertically to save space and which, according to Wccftech, can raise chip density by 30 to 50 percent. Wccftech says this would put CXMT about two years ahead of Samsung, whose use of the design is reported to start in 2028, but it is the company's own claim and Wccftech expects the first version to be only a partial form of the design.
notes: Read in full via fulltext. Source credit: Wccftech's own article, relaying a speech by CXMT's president; the speech date is not stated and no other outlet carrying it was found. The Samsung 2028 date comes from an X post quoted by Wccftech.
